questions.q: What is the capital city of Senegal?
questions.e: Dakar is the capital of Senegal.

questions.q: Which ocean lies west of Senegal?
questions.e: Senegal has a coastline on the Atlantic Ocean.

questions.q: Which language is the official language of Senegal?
questions.e: French is Senegal’s official language; many national languages are also spoken.

questions.q: Gorée Island is located near which city?
questions.e: Gorée Island lies close to Dakar.

questions.q: Which large river forms part of Senegal’s northern border?
questions.e: The Senegal River runs along part of the border with Mauritania.

questions.q: Which Senegalese national park is known for wildlife and lies in the southeast?
questions.e: Niokolo-Koba is a major national park in southeastern Senegal.

questions.q: Which country is directly south of Senegal and is surrounded by Senegal on most sides?
questions.e: The Gambia follows the Gambia River and is surrounded by Senegal except for its Atlantic coast.

questions.q: What is the name of the westernmost point of mainland Africa, near Dakar?
questions.e: Pointe des Almadies is near Dakar on the western edge of mainland Africa.

questions.q: Which Senegalese region is especially known for its mangroves and river delta?
questions.e: The Sine-Saloum area includes an important delta and mangrove ecosystem.

questions.q: What is a baobab?
questions.e: The baobab is a large tree found in Africa.

questions.q: Which country is famous for the ancient city of Timbuktu?
questions.e: Timbuktu is a historic city in Mali.

questions.q: Which African country has the city of Mombasa on its Indian Ocean coast?
questions.e: Mombasa is a coastal city in Kenya.

questions.q: Mount Kilimanjaro is in which country?
questions.e: Mount Kilimanjaro is in northeastern Tanzania.

questions.q: Which waterfall lies on the border of Zambia and Zimbabwe?
questions.e: Victoria Falls is on the Zambezi River at the Zambia–Zimbabwe border.

questions.q: Which is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.e: The Sahara is the world’s largest hot desert.

questions.q: What is the capital of Kenya?
questions.e: Nairobi is the capital of Kenya.

questions.q: Which sea separates northeastern Africa from the Arabian Peninsula?
questions.e: The Red Sea lies between northeastern Africa and the Arabian Peninsula.

questions.q: Which country became independent from Britain in 1957 and was formerly called the Gold Coast?
questions.e: The former Gold Coast became independent Ghana in 1957.

questions.q: Lake Victoria borders Kenya, Uganda and which other country?
questions.e: Lake Victoria is shared by Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya.

questions.q: Which African country is home to the ancient rock-hewn churches of Lalibela?
questions.e: Lalibela’s rock-hewn churches are in Ethiopia.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a national park?
questions.e: National parks help conserve habitats and wildlife.

questions.q: Which animal is the largest land mammal in Africa?
questions.e: The African elephant is the largest land mammal on land.

questions.q: Which continent is directly north of Senegal across the Mediterranean Sea?
questions.e: Europe lies north of Africa across the Mediterranean Sea.

questions.q: Which river flows through Egypt and empties into the Mediterranean Sea?
questions.e: The Nile flows north through Egypt to the Mediterranean.

questions.q: Which Senegalese dish was added to UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2021?
questions.e: UNESCO lists Ceebu Jën as a culinary art of Senegal.

questions.q: Xooy is a divination ceremony associated with which Senegalese community?
questions.e: UNESCO describes Xooy as a Serer divination ceremony.

questions.q: Kankurang is described by UNESCO as which kind of heritage?
questions.e: UNESCO lists Kankurang as a Manding initiatory rite.

questions.q: The Stone Circles of Senegambia are shared by Senegal and which country?
questions.e: The UNESCO site includes components in Senegal and The Gambia.

questions.q: Which two named stone-circle groups are in Senegal?
questions.e: UNESCO locates Wanar and Sine Ngayène in Senegal.

questions.q: Which two named stone-circle groups are in The Gambia?
questions.e: UNESCO locates Wassu and Kerbatch in The Gambia.

questions.q: What are many of the mounds associated with the Senegambian stone circles?
questions.e: UNESCO describes associated tumuli as burial mounds.

questions.q: Which three peoples are named in the Bassari Country World Heritage site?
questions.e: The UNESCO site's name identifies the Bassari, Fula and Bedik landscapes.

questions.q: In which part of Senegal is Bassari Country located?
questions.e: UNESCO locates Bassari Country in south-eastern Senegal.

questions.q: What is a feature of the Bassari landscape described by UNESCO?
questions.e: UNESCO describes terraces and rice paddies among Bassari villages.

questions.q: What is characteristic of many Bedik village houses?
questions.e: UNESCO describes Bedik villages with huts and steep thatched roofs.

questions.q: What is the Saloum Delta especially known for in its cultural landscape?
questions.e: UNESCO highlights shell mounds and coastal livelihoods in the delta.

questions.q: What kind of water is found in parts of the Saloum Delta?
o: Water with no salt at all
questions.e: UNESCO describes the delta's water as brackish.

questions.q: What traditional activities helped shape the Saloum Delta landscape?
questions.e: UNESCO describes shellfish gathering and fishing practices.

questions.q: Where is the Island of Saint-Louis situated?
o: At the source of the Nile
In the middle of Lake Victoria
At the mouth of the Senegal River
On the coast of The Gambia River
questions.e: UNESCO places Saint-Louis at the mouth of the Senegal River.

questions.q: Which city became Senegal’s capital after the role moved from Saint-Louis?
questions.e: Dakar is Senegal's national capital.

questions.q: Which Senegalese island was inscribed on the World Heritage List in 1978?
questions.e: UNESCO lists Gorée as inscribed in 1978.

questions.q: In which year was the Island of Saint-Louis inscribed on UNESCO’s World Heritage List?
questions.e: UNESCO records the Island of Saint-Louis inscription in 2000.

questions.q: In which year was the Saloum Delta inscribed on the World Heritage List?
questions.e: UNESCO records the Saloum Delta inscription in 2011.

questions.q: In which year were the Stone Circles of Senegambia inscribed?
questions.e: UNESCO records the inscription in 2006.

questions.q: Which Senegalese World Heritage site is known for a bird sanctuary?
questions.e: Djoudj is listed by UNESCO as a national bird sanctuary.

questions.q: What kind of heritage is Ceebu Jën recognized as?
questions.e: UNESCO lists Ceebu Jën as a culinary art.

questions.q: What do UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscapes often show?
o: Only the weather of a place
How people and their environment interact
questions.e: Cultural landscapes reflect relationships between communities and their environment.

questions.q: What is a tumulus in the context of the Senegambian stone circles?
o: A mound associated with a burial
questions.e: UNESCO describes tumuli as burial mounds.

questions.q: Near which Ghanaian city are the Asante Traditional Buildings located?
questions.e: UNESCO locates the buildings near Kumasi.

questions.q: Which materials are named for the Asante Traditional Buildings?
questions.e: UNESCO lists earth, wood and straw.

questions.q: What decorative feature appears on Asante building walls?
questions.e: UNESCO notes decorative bas-reliefs.

questions.q: In which country are the Royal Palaces of Abomey?
questions.e: Abomey is in Benin.

questions.q: How many kings succeeded one another in Abomey between 1625 and 1900?
questions.e: UNESCO counts twelve successive kings.

questions.q: What material formed the traditional walls around Abomey palace compounds?
questions.e: UNESCO describes walls made of cob.

questions.q: Lamu Old Town is on the coast of which country?
questions.e: Lamu is on Kenya’s East African coast.

questions.q: Which historic culture is especially represented by Lamu Old Town?
questions.e: UNESCO describes Lamu as a Swahili settlement.

questions.q: Which pair of materials was used in historic buildings in Lamu?
questions.e: UNESCO names coral stone and mangrove timber.

questions.q: Great Zimbabwe is located in which country?
questions.e: The monument is in Zimbabwe.

questions.q: Which people are associated with the founding of Great Zimbabwe?
questions.e: UNESCO identifies the builders as the Shona.

questions.q: Aksum is an ancient site in which country?
questions.e: Aksum is in northern Ethiopia.

questions.q: Stone Town is a historic settlement in which country?
questions.e: Stone Town is on Zanzibar, part of Tanzania.

questions.q: Which coastal culture is represented by Stone Town?
questions.e: UNESCO describes it as a Swahili coastal trading town.

questions.q: Which materials are named in the construction of Stone Town buildings?
questions.e: UNESCO names coral stone and mangrove timber.

questions.q: Which set of cultural influences is reflected in Stone Town?
questions.e: UNESCO describes these influences in the town’s architecture.

questions.q: Timbuktu is in which West African country?
questions.e: Timbuktu is a historic city in Mali.

questions.q: What was Sankore in Timbuktu?
questions.e: UNESCO describes Sankore as a university and learning centre.

questions.q: Which goods were traded in Timbuktu’s historic markets?
questions.e: UNESCO notes manuscript, salt and gold trade.

questions.q: Which mosque is one of Timbuktu’s three historic great mosques?
questions.e: Sankore is one of the three mosques listed by UNESCO.

questions.q: The Old Towns of Djenné are in which country?
questions.e: Djenné is in Mali.

questions.q: Which building material is especially important in Djenné’s historic architecture?
questions.e: UNESCO highlights the use of earth in its architecture.

questions.q: Why were many traditional houses in Djenné built on raised mounds?
o: To be closer to the sea
To reduce the effect of seasonal floods
questions.e: UNESCO notes that the mounds protect houses from seasonal floods.

questions.q: Which historic trade helped Djenné grow as a market centre?
questions.e: UNESCO describes Djenné as an important link in the trans-Saharan gold trade.

questions.q: Robben Island is off the coast of which country?
questions.e: Robben Island is a South African heritage site.

questions.q: What were some historic uses of Robben Island?
questions.e: UNESCO lists these uses across different periods.

questions.q: What does Robben Island’s heritage symbolize?
o: The start of the Swahili language
questions.e: UNESCO links the site to this symbolic history.

questions.q: What type of prison building is prominent on Robben Island?
o: A maximum-security prison for political prisoners
questions.e: UNESCO identifies the maximum-security political prison.

questions.q: Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape is in which country?
questions.e: UNESCO identifies Mapungubwe as a South African site.

questions.q: Which two rivers meet at the Mapungubwe landscape?
questions.e: UNESCO locates it at the Limpopo–Shashe confluence.

questions.q: Mapungubwe is described as an early kingdom in which region?
questions.e: UNESCO calls it the first indigenous kingdom in Southern Africa.

questions.q: Which valuable resources supported Mapungubwe’s trade?
questions.e: UNESCO says its hinterland supplied gold and ivory.

questions.q: Which climate change contributed to Mapungubwe’s decline?
o: A change in monsoon winds in Asia
questions.e: UNESCO connects the kingdom’s decline to drier conditions.

questions.q: Which historic settlement is near the borders of South Africa, Zimbabwe and Botswana?
questions.e: UNESCO places Mapungubwe where those three countries meet.

questions.q: Which kind of town is Stone Town described as?
questions.e: UNESCO describes this settlement as a Swahili trading town.

questions.q: What feature is found on some Stone Town buildings?
questions.e: UNESCO describes elaborately carved doors.

questions.q: Which country is home to the Great Zimbabwe National Monument?
questions.e: UNESCO locates the monument in Zimbabwe.

questions.q: Which people built the civilization represented at Great Zimbabwe?
questions.e: UNESCO describes Great Zimbabwe as a testimony to Shona civilization.

questions.q: Between which centuries did the Shona civilization at Great Zimbabwe flourish?
questions.e: UNESCO dates this civilization from the 11th to the 15th century.

questions.q: What was Great Zimbabwe during the Middle Ages?
questions.e: UNESCO describes it as an important trading centre.

questions.q: Lalibela’s rock-hewn churches are in which country?
questions.e: Lalibela is in the heart of Ethiopia.

questions.q: How many medieval monolithic churches are at Lalibela?
questions.e: UNESCO identifies eleven churches carved from rock.

questions.q: What makes Lalibela’s churches especially distinctive?
questions.e: The churches were carved directly out of rock.

questions.q: Lalibela is still an important place for what?
questions.e: UNESCO describes Lalibela as a place of pilgrimage and devotion.

questions.q: Aksum is an ancient archaeological site in which country?
questions.e: Aksum is in northern Ethiopia.

questions.q: Which monuments are among the ruins at Aksum?
questions.e: UNESCO lists obelisks and giant stelae among its monuments.

questions.q: The ancient Kingdom of Aksum controlled trade connected to which sea?
questions.e: Aksumite fleets controlled trade through the Red Sea.

questions.q: Which historic port is associated with Aksum’s maritime trade?
questions.e: UNESCO names Adulis as the port connected to Aksumite trade.

questions.q: Fort Jesus is in which Kenyan coastal city?
questions.e: Fort Jesus stands in Mombasa.

questions.q: Who built Fort Jesus at the end of the 16th century?
questions.e: UNESCO says the Portuguese built the fort in 1593–1596.

questions.q: What was the main purpose of Fort Jesus when it was built?
questions.e: It was built to protect the port of Mombasa.

questions.q: On what kind of natural feature was Fort Jesus built?
questions.e: UNESCO places the fort on a spur of coral rock.

questions.q: Which architect designed Fort Jesus?
questions.e: UNESCO attributes its design to Giovanni Battista Cairati.

questions.q: Which type of architecture is Fort Jesus an example of?
questions.e: UNESCO calls it an outstanding example of 16th-century Portuguese fortification.

questions.q: Which groups’ cultural influences are visible in Fort Jesus’s history?
o: African, Arab, Turkish, Persian and European
questions.e: UNESCO describes exchanges among these peoples around the port.

questions.q: Which city was the powerful ancient Kingdom of Aksum’s heart?
questions.e: The ruins of Aksum mark the heart of the ancient kingdom.

questions.q: Lalibela is described as a ‘New Jerusalem’ from which century?
questions.e: UNESCO describes the churches as a 13th-century ‘New Jerusalem’.

questions.q: The Great Zimbabwe site covers nearly how much land?
questions.e: UNESCO gives an area of nearly 80 hectares.

questions.q: What kind of cultural landscape surrounds Lalibela’s churches?
o: A mountainous region near a traditional village
questions.e: UNESCO places the churches in a mountain region near a traditional village.

questions.q: Which building tradition is represented by the monumental ruins of Great Zimbabwe?
questions.e: The monument is a testimony to Shona civilization.

questions.q: Which four Senegalese towns made up the historic "Four Communes" under French rule?
questions.e: Les Quatre Communes étaient Dakar, Saint-Louis, Gorée et Rufisque.

questions.q: Blaise Diagne, elected deputy in 1914, was notable for being the first ...?
o: Black African elected to the French Parliament
questions.e: Blaise Diagne fut le premier Africain noir élu député à l'Assemblée nationale française.

questions.q: The 1960 Mali Federation briefly united Senegal with which other territory?
questions.e: La Fédération du Mali unissait le Sénégal et le Soudan français, aujourd'hui le Mali.

questions.q: Senghor's long rule as president ended in 1980 when he did what, unusually for the region at the time?
o: He was overthrown by the army
questions.e: Senghor a démissionné volontairement en 1980, un geste rare à l'époque.

questions.q: Abdou Diouf, Senegal's second president, later became secretary-general of which international organisation?
o: The Organisation internationale de la Francophonie
questions.e: Abdou Diouf a dirigé l'Organisation internationale de la Francophonie après sa présidence.

questions.q: Abdoulaye Wade came to power in 2000 after defeating which long-ruling party?
questions.e: Wade a battu le Parti Socialiste, au pouvoir depuis l'indépendance.

questions.q: In which year did Macky Sall first become president of Senegal?
questions.e: Macky Sall est devenu président du Sénégal en 2012.

questions.q: Bassirou Diomaye Faye won the 2024 presidential election while representing which kind of political coalition?
o: An opposition coalition linked to Ousmane Sonko's party
questions.e: Faye représentait une coalition d'opposition liée au parti d'Ousmane Sonko.

questions.q: What was Senegal called administratively within French West Africa before independence?
o: A colony within the Afrique Occidentale Française (AOF)
questions.e: Le Sénégal était une colonie au sein de l'AOF, fédération de colonies françaises.

questions.q: Which Senegalese region has Kaolack as its capital and is closely tied to groundnut trade?
questions.e: La région de Kaolack est historiquement liée au commerce de l'arachide.

questions.q: Tambacounda region, in eastern Senegal, is known for sharing a border with which two countries?
questions.e: Tambacounda est frontalière du Mali et de la Guinée.

questions.q: The Senegal River basin is shared by Senegal, Mauritania, Mali and which other country?
questions.e: Le bassin du fleuve Sénégal est partagé par quatre pays, dont la Guinée.

questions.q: Which Senegalese region contains the historic town of Podor, on the Senegal River?
questions.e: Podor se trouve dans la région de Saint-Louis, le long du fleuve.

questions.q: The Niayes is a narrow coastal zone in Senegal particularly known for growing ...?
questions.e: La zone des Niayes est réputée pour le maraîchage.

questions.q: Senegal's highest points are found mainly in which south-eastern region, near the Guinean border?
questions.e: Les points les plus élevés du Sénégal se trouvent surtout dans la région de Kédougou.

questions.q: Senegal's central bank for the West African CFA franc zone is based in which country?
questions.e: La Banque Centrale des États de l'Afrique de l'Ouest (BCEAO) a son siège à Dakar.

questions.q: Which international organisation groups Senegal with other countries sharing the West African CFA franc?
o: UEMOA (West African Economic and Monetary Union)
questions.e: L'UEMOA regroupe les pays utilisant le franc CFA ouest-africain.

questions.q: Senegal's main electricity company, often discussed in the news, is called ...?
questions.e: La SENELEC est la société nationale d'électricité du Sénégal.

questions.q: In recent years, Senegal has started producing which natural resources offshore, boosting its economy?
questions.e: Le Sénégal a commencé l'exploitation de gisements de pétrole et de gaz offshore.

questions.q: Which crop processing industry, linked to groundnuts, has long been important in Senegal's economy?
questions.e: La production d'huile d'arachide est une industrie traditionnelle importante.

questions.q: Remittances sent home by Senegalese people living abroad make up a significant part of the country's ...?
questions.e: Les transferts de la diaspora représentent une part importante des revenus du pays.

questions.q: The Mouride brotherhood was founded in the late 19th century by which religious leader?
questions.e: Cheikh Amadou Bamba a fondé la confrérie mouride à la fin du XIXe siècle.

questions.q: The Tidiane brotherhood in Senegal is closely associated with which holy city?
questions.e: La confrérie tidiane est fortement associée à la ville de Tivaouane.

questions.q: In Senegal, the term "baye fall" refers to followers known for their devotion within which brotherhood?
questions.e: Les baye fall sont des disciples particuliers de la confrérie mouride.

questions.q: Senegal's constitution describes the state as what, regarding religion?
questions.e: La Constitution sénégalaise définit un État laïc, malgré la majorité musulmane.

questions.q: Which festival in Senegal, shared across religions, involves children going door to door asking for treats?
questions.e: Le Tamkharit (ou Kaw-Kaw) ressemble à une tradition où les enfants réclament des friandises.

questions.q: Senegal's men's basketball team is historically one of the strongest on which continent?
questions.e: Le Sénégal possède l'une des meilleures équipes de basketball en Afrique.

questions.q: Senegalese-born NBA player Gorgui Dieng played professionally in which country's basketball league?
questions.e: Gorgui Dieng a joué en NBA, la grande ligue américaine de basketball.

questions.q: The 2021 Africa Cup of Nations football title, won by Senegal, was played with the final against which country?
questions.e: Le Sénégal a battu l'Égypte en finale de la CAN 2021.

questions.q: Senegalese wrestler Balla Gaye 2 is known for competing in which traditional sport?
questions.e: Balla Gaye 2 est un lutteur célèbre de la lutte traditionnelle sénégalaise.

questions.q: Senegal has produced several world-class athletes in which Olympic combat sport, besides wrestling?
questions.e: Le Sénégal a produit des judokas de haut niveau sur la scène internationale.

questions.q: Which historic Senegalese university, founded in 1957, is one of the oldest in French-speaking Africa?
questions.e: L'Université Cheikh Anta Diop de Dakar, fondée en 1957, est l'une des plus anciennes d'Afrique francophone.

questions.q: Cheikh Anta Diop, after whom Dakar's main university is named, was known as a scholar of which subject?
questions.e: Cheikh Anta Diop était un historien connu pour ses travaux sur l'Égypte ancienne et l'Afrique.

questions.q: What is the usual language of instruction in most Senegalese public schools?
questions.e: Le français reste la langue d'enseignement principale dans les écoles publiques.

questions.q: Daara is the Senegalese term for a traditional school focused mainly on teaching ...?
questions.e: Le daara est une école traditionnelle consacrée à l'enseignement coranique.

questions.q: Which Senegalese filmmaker directed "Touki Bouki", an influential African film from 1973?
questions.e: Djibril Diop Mambéty a réalisé « Touki Bouki », film culte de 1973.

questions.q: Which prize, awarded at the Cannes Film Festival, was won by Senegalese director Mati Diop for "Atlantique"?
questions.e: Mati Diop a remporté le Grand Prix de Cannes pour « Atlantique » en 2019.

questions.q: The Senegalese sabar drumming tradition is often linked to which social events?
questions.e: Le sabar accompagne souvent les mariages, baptêmes et fêtes.

questions.q: Rapper and singer Didier Awadi, from the group Positive Black Soul, helped develop which music genre in Senegal?
questions.e: Didier Awadi est une figure majeure du hip-hop sénégalais.

questions.q: Senegal created the Niokolo-Koba National Park partly to protect which large mammal under threat?
questions.e: Le parc a été créé notamment pour protéger éléphants et lions.

questions.q: Which coastal Senegalese wetland area is internationally recognised under the Ramsar Convention for its importance to birds?
questions.e: Le site du Djoudj est reconnu internationalement pour son importance pour les oiseaux migrateurs.

questions.q: Desertification and reduced rainfall have been challenges for farmers in which part of Senegal?
questions.e: La désertification touche surtout la zone sahélienne du nord du Sénégal.

questions.q: The Great Green Wall initiative, which Senegal supports, aims mainly to fight ...?
questions.e: La Grande Muraille Verte vise à lutter contre la désertification dans le Sahel.

questions.q: Senegal has historically sent many peacekeeping troops to support which type of international missions?
questions.e: Le Sénégal est un contributeur régulier aux missions de maintien de la paix de l'ONU.

questions.q: Which former Senegalese president became head of the African Union Commission in 2012?
o: No Senegalese president led the AU Commission; it was a Gabonese/South African mix
Macky Sall became AU chairperson in 2022
questions.e: Macky Sall a présidé l'Union africaine (poste tournant) en 2022.

questions.q: Senegal maintains strong historic and cultural ties with France partly because of ...?
o: A shared currency with the Euro directly
Being part of the European Union
Its colonial history and shared use of French
questions.e: Les liens avec la France découlent surtout de l'histoire coloniale et de la langue française.

questions.q: Which Senegalese city, besides Dakar, has an international airport that opened in 2017?
questions.e: L'aéroport international Blaise Diagne, ouvert en 2017, se trouve à Diass.

questions.q: What role did Dakar's old Yoff airport play before the new one opened?
o: It was the main international airport of Senegal
It was a military base only
questions.e: L'aéroport de Yoff a longtemps été le principal aéroport international du pays.

questions.q: Which Senegalese export has historically depended heavily on rainfall levels, making farmers vulnerable to drought?
questions.e: Les récoltes d'arachide et de mil dépendent fortement de la pluviométrie.

questions.q: The Senegalese currency, the CFA franc, is pegged to which major foreign currency?
questions.e: Le franc CFA ouest-africain est arrimé à l'euro.

questions.q: Which organisation issues the banknotes used in Senegal and other UEMOA countries?
o: The BCEAO (Central Bank of West African States)
questions.e: La BCEAO émet la monnaie commune des pays de l'UEMOA.

questions.q: Dakar's historic railway station was an important stop on the line connecting Dakar to which other West African capital?
questions.e: La ligne ferroviaire reliait historiquement Dakar à Bamako, au Mali.

questions.q: Which Senegalese region, bordering The Gambia to the north, is important for groundnut and millet farming?
questions.e: La région de Kaolack, au nord de la Gambie, est agricole, notamment pour l'arachide.

questions.q: Senegal's rainy season, called "hivernage", usually lasts from around June to ...?
questions.e: L'hivernage dure généralement de juin à octobre environ.

questions.q: The harmattan, a dry and dusty wind affecting Senegal, originates mainly from which region?
questions.e: L'harmattan est un vent sec et poussiéreux venant du Sahara.

questions.q: Which Senegalese port city historically specialised in exporting groundnuts during the colonial period?
questions.e: Rufisque était un port important pour l'exportation de l'arachide à l'époque coloniale.

questions.q: The Lebou community traditionally practises a system of local self-governance around Dakar known for having a ...?
o: Formal parliament elected by all Senegal
Traditional chief called the Serigne Ndakarou
questions.e: Les Lébous ont une organisation traditionnelle autour d'un chef, le Serigne Ndakarou.

questions.q: Which Senegalese artist is especially known for "recycled art", using everyday objects to create sculptures?
o: Artists from the Suitcase/Récup' art movement in Dakar
No Senegalese artist works with recycled materials
questions.e: Des artistes sénégalais utilisent des objets recyclés pour créer des œuvres, notamment à Dakar.

questions.q: The griot tradition in Senegal is often passed down through which method?
o: Family lineage, from parents to children
questions.e: La tradition griotte se transmet généralement de génération en génération au sein des familles.

questions.q: Senegalese wrestling matches (laamb) traditionally take place in an arena called a ...?
questions.e: Les combats de lutte se déroulent dans une arène appelée « arène » en français.

questions.q: Which Senegalese musical instrument, a type of xylophone, is used in some traditional performances?
questions.e: Le balafon, sorte de xylophone, est utilisé dans certaines musiques traditionnelles ouest-africaines.

questions.q: Senegal's national library and archives, important for preserving documents, are mainly located in which city?
questions.e: Les principales bibliothèques et archives nationales se trouvent à Dakar.

questions.q: Which Senegalese newspaper, among the most widely read, is published in French?
questions.e: Le Soleil est un grand quotidien sénégalais publié en français.

questions.q: Senegal's national television broadcaster is commonly known by which abbreviation?
questions.e: La RTS est le principal diffuseur public du Sénégal.

questions.q: Which Senegalese city hosts an important annual Islamic gathering called the Gamou, alongside Tivaouane?
questions.e: Médina Baye, près de Kaolack, est aussi un centre important pour le Gamou.

questions.q: Which Senegalese wrestler-turned-businessman, Mohamed Ndao "Tyson", became well known for his career in which sport?
questions.e: Tyson est un ancien lutteur sénégalais très populaire.

questions.q: Which West African regional currency reform project, discussed since the 2010s, would eventually replace the CFA franc?
questions.e: L'éco est le nom prévu pour une future monnaie régionale ouest-africaine.

questions.q: Senegal's main stock exchange activities are connected to which larger West African regional exchange?
o: The BRVM (Bourse Régionale des Valeurs Mobilières)
questions.e: La BRVM, basée à Abidjan, couvre les pays de l'UEMOA, dont le Sénégal.

questions.q: Which Senegalese region is particularly affected by coastal erosion threatening fishing villages?
o: Areas along the Atlantic coast, such as Saint-Louis
questions.e: L'érosion côtière menace des villages de pêcheurs, notamment près de Saint-Louis.

questions.q: Senegal's main mobile phone and telecom companies include Orange and which other well-known operator?
questions.e: Free (anciennement Tigo) est un opérateur télécom important au Sénégal, avec Orange.

questions.q: What role does the River Senegal play for farmers in the north of the country?
o: It is frozen most of the year
It provides water for irrigation of rice and other crops
questions.e: Le fleuve Sénégal permet l'irrigation de cultures comme le riz.

questions.q: Which Senegalese sport, besides wrestling and football, has grown in popularity with national leagues and youth programmes?
questions.e: Le basketball a une ligue nationale active et des programmes pour les jeunes.

questions.q: Senegal has taken part in which pan-African sporting event held every four years, besides the Africa Cup of Nations?
questions.e: Le Sénégal participe aux Jeux africains, un événement sportif continental.

questions.q: Senegal's main public university system includes Cheikh Anta Diop University in Dakar and which other major university, in Saint-Louis?
questions.e: L'Université Gaston Berger de Saint-Louis est une autre grande université publique.

questions.q: What does the acronym BFEM, important in the Senegalese school system, stand for?
o: Bachelor of Fine Education in Mathematics
questions.e: Le BFEM est le Brevet de Fin d'Études Moyennes, un diplôme de collège au Sénégal.

questions.q: Which national exam, taken at the end of secondary school in Senegal, allows access to university?
questions.e: Le baccalauréat sanctionne la fin des études secondaires au Sénégal.

questions.q: The CFA franc used in Senegal is distinct from the Central African CFA franc, which is used in a different regional group called ...?
o: CEMAC (Central African Economic and Monetary Community)
questions.e: La zone CEMAC utilise un franc CFA différent de celui de l'UEMOA.

questions.q: Senegal's main deep-sea fishing exports often go to markets in which continent, alongside regional African markets?
questions.e: Une grande partie des exportations de poisson sénégalais va vers l'Europe.

questions.q: Which famous Senegalese boxer represented the country internationally in the sport of boxing?
o: Only wrestlers represent Senegal in combat sports
Boxers from Senegal have competed at continental and world level
No Senegalese boxer has ever competed internationally
questions.e: Le Sénégal a produit des boxeurs ayant participé à des compétitions internationales.

questions.q: Which Senegalese singer and songwriter is known for songs blending mbalax with reggae influences?
o: Only classical composers exist in Senegal
Awadi, Daara J, and similar artists blend genres
No reggae-influenced music exists in Senegal
questions.e: Plusieurs artistes sénégalais mélangent mbalax, reggae et hip-hop.

questions.q: Senegal's film industry has historically produced work recognised at international festivals such as ...?
questions.e: Des films sénégalais ont été reconnus à Cannes et au FESPACO, grand festival africain du cinéma.

questions.q: FESPACO, a major pan-African film festival often attended by Senegalese filmmakers, is held in which country?
questions.e: Le FESPACO se tient à Ouagadougou, au Burkina Faso.

questions.q: What is the traditional Senegalese wedding custom in which the groom's family offers gifts to the bride's family called?
questions.e: Il existe une tradition de dot offerte par la famille du marié.

questions.q: Which Senegalese dessert, made with couscous, milk and sometimes raisins, is often served at celebrations?
questions.e: Le thiakry est un dessert traditionnel souvent servi lors de fêtes.

questions.q: Senegal's main maritime fishing fleet mainly operates from which type of boats, especially for small-scale fishers?
questions.e: Les pirogues en bois sont le principal moyen de pêche artisanale au Sénégal.

questions.q: Which Senegalese region is particularly known for cotton production, alongside groundnuts?
questions.e: La région de Tambacounda produit notamment du coton.

questions.q: The Confédération Nationale des Travailleurs du Sénégal is an example of which kind of organisation?
questions.e: C'est une grande confédération syndicale sénégalaise.

questions.q: Senegal's civil service and courts mainly operate using a legal system influenced by which tradition?
questions.e: Le système juridique sénégalais est largement influencé par le droit civil français.

questions.q: Which Senegalese government ministry would typically be responsible for managing national parks like Niokolo-Koba?
o: The ministry in charge of environment and nature protection
questions.e: La gestion des parcs nationaux relève du ministère chargé de l'environnement.

questions.q: Dakar's rapidly growing suburbs, including Pikine and Guédiawaye, are known mainly for being ...?
questions.e: Pikine et Guédiawaye sont des banlieues très peuplées de Dakar.

questions.q: Which Senegalese region includes Thiès, often called the country's second-largest city by some measures?
questions.e: Thiès, importante ville industrielle, se trouve dans la région du même nom.

questions.q: Senegal's railway and port infrastructure historically supported the export of which mineral besides phosphates?
o: Iron ore (more recently, from the Falémé area)
questions.e: Du minerai de fer est exploité dans la région de la Falémé, à l'est.

questions.q: Which Senegalese organisation represents the country at the Olympic Games?
questions.e: Le Comité National Olympique Sénégalais représente le pays aux Jeux Olympiques.

questions.q: Senegal's main container port, handling most of the country's maritime trade, is located in which city?
questions.e: Le port de Dakar gère la majeure partie du commerce maritime du pays.

questions.q: Which Senegalese region hosts the annual Kaay Fecc festival, celebrating traditional dance?
questions.e: Le festival Kaay Fecc, dédié à la danse, se tient notamment à Dakar.

questions.q: Senegal's radio stations, an important source of information in rural areas, often broadcast in which languages, besides French?
o: Local languages such as Wolof and Pulaar
questions.e: De nombreuses radios sénégalaises diffusent en wolof, pulaar et d'autres langues locales.

questions.q: Which Senegalese region is known for the historic town of Kayar, an important fishing centre?
questions.e: Kayar, important centre de pêche, se trouve dans la région de Thiès.

questions.q: A "Grand Magal" pilgrimage to Touba commemorates an event in the life of which religious figure?
o: Cheikh Amadou Bamba's departure into exile
questions.e: Le Grand Magal commémore le départ en exil de Cheikh Amadou Bamba.

questions.q: Senegal's traditional wrestling championship often crowns a top fighter with the title ...?
questions.e: Le titre honorifique de « Roi des Arènes » est attribué au meilleur lutteur.

questions.q: Which Senegalese city is historically known as a centre for Quranic education and Islamic scholarship, alongside Touba?
questions.e: Médina Baye est un centre réputé pour l'enseignement coranique.
